title: Sage Vishvamitra's Request
captions: King Dasharatha hurried to welcome the sage Vishvamitra and bowed low before him.
“Great sage, your visit is a blessing,” said the king. “Ask for anything, and I promise it shall be yours.”
“Demons keep spoiling my sacred fire ceremony in the forest,” said Vishvamitra. “Send your son Rama with me to protect it.”
The king's heart sank. “Rama is still a boy! Take me and my whole army, but please do not ask for my son.”
Then the wise Vasishtha spoke gently. “A king must keep his word. Trust the sage. Rama will be safe, and he will learn great things.”
Dasharatha took a deep breath and kept his promise. He blessed Rama and Lakshmana and placed them in the sage's care.
With bows on their shoulders, the two young princes followed Vishvamitra out of Ayodhya and into their first great adventure.
lesson: King Dasharatha loved Rama more than his own life, so keeping his promise was very hard. But in our tradition a promise is sacred. Satya means speaking the truth and doing what you said you would do, even when it is difficult. The king kept his word, and he trusted his guru's advice.
card_lesson: The king's promise was very hard to keep, but he kept it. Satya means speaking the truth and doing what you said you would do, even when it is difficult.
question: Have you ever made a promise that was hard to keep? What did you do?
